class.name: PhysXRockDust3D
class.brief_description: Rockfall dust simulated in NVIDIA Flow.
class.description: Takes the dust a [RockField3D]'s falling and broken stones throw up (where their pieces hit, break and slide) within [member near_range] of [member follow_target], and feeds it into a [PhysXFlow3D] of its own as short bursts through a pool of sphere emitters. The dust swells out of each impact and runs on along the piece's path. It is heavier than the air, rests on the terrain floor (the field's generator), curls round the moving pieces, drifts with the [WeatherMap3D]'s wind and fades over tens of seconds. A [RockField3D] with [member RockField3D.rockfall_dust] on makes one itself.

Off: no new dust (what is in the air settles).
How fast the cloud swells out of an impact (emitter divergence, per second).
